newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders seek 0.2-1.0 mln tns EU wheat for Africa.
newsitem.headline: Traders seek 0.2-1.0 mln tns EU wheat for Africa.

text.p: Grain traders have made provisional applications for 200,000 to one million tonnes of European Union wheat exports to a new target group of African countries to be carried out by June 30, European grain officials said.
The applications are subject to contracts and come under a long-term export scheme launched by the EU last Thursday to provide special relief for traditional African customers.

Under so-called Article Nine rules, traders must supply sales contracts to receive the EU export licences. These are available with special refunds of 12 Ecus per tonne up to the end of the year and 19 Ecus from January onwards. They are valid until the end of the season on June 30, 1997.
"We should have the final figure in two weeks," one official said on Wednesday.

Under a similar new scheme which provides traders a licence valid for nearly five months, but without having to show contracts in advance, the industry has applied for 150,000 tonnes of wheat exports since last Thursday, officials said.
The base refund of 12 Ecus per tonne is about five Ecus per tonne higher than the latest ordinary refund given out last week for shipments to any non-EU importing country.
It is a narrower version of the help traditionally given by the EU to the African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries protected under the Lome trade conventions.
Both European and U.S. officials said this week the refund for Africa was unlikely to fuel tensions with Washington over EU wheat subsidies since the ACP measures had long been recognised.
European officials and traders said care had also been taken to exclude U.S. markets from the list of targeted importers.
